summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY. Builds and deploys C/C++ and Python software across NVIDIA Jetson, STM32, and Linux platforms, from FreeRTOS-based microcontroller control with interrupt-driven UART peripherals to ROS 2 (Humble/Noetic) kinematics validated against MoveIt/RViz, plus systemd deployment and static-IP networking for reliable multi-device robot software. Comfortable working across hardware and software boundaries, closing integration gaps through structured debugging, and documenting findings for a team.

Linux & Tools: systemd service management (unit files, auto-restart, non-root isolation)

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove for hands-free cursor control integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Developed a Python GUI using PyQt and Matplotlib for real-time data acquisition and experimental visualization in a laboratory environment.
Used GitLab for version control and JupyterHub for collaborative data analysis and technical documentation.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Built a voice-controlled, vision-guided robotic pick-and-place system across a three-layer pipeline (Flutter client, Flask-SocketIO edge server, NVIDIA Jetson+Arduino controller) linked by a unified WebSocket fabric.
Deployed the Jetson-side arm bridge as a systemd service with static-IP networking for reliable multi-device WebSocket registration; configured XRDP for remote administration of the headless Jetson.

Resolved 11 integration failures across the C/C++/Python stack (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture); achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) at ~11.5s end-to-end latency.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects, sending control commands to an STM32 microcontroller over UART.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART commands and user override.
Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED distance visualization.

projects.name: ROS-Based Robotic Arm (AL5B & UR5e)
bullets: Derived DH tables and hand-computed full forward kinematic chains for a 6-DoF UR5e and 5-DoF AL5B; validated against MoveIt and RViz URDF models in ROS 2 Humble and ROS Noetic.
Planned and executed collision-free pick-and-place trajectories on a physical UR5e via the UR ROS 2 driver; AL5B repeatability measured at <2mm over 10 trials.

awards: 1st Prize, CanSat Workshop — Arduino Nano atmospheric data collection during free fall (2023)
Ranked 10th, Robocon — National-level robotics competition among 45 universities (2022)
